title: Email & Domain
description: Domain identity, email delivery, and address-normalization risks.

attacks.name: Email spoofing
attacks.desc: Weak SPF, DKIM, or DMARC policy can make forged mail appear to come from a trusted domain.
attacks.prevention: Publish and enforce SPF, DKIM, and DMARC policies, and monitor authentication failures.

attacks.name: Display-name spoofing
attacks.desc: A trusted-looking display name can hide an unrelated sender address from a casual reader.
attacks.prevention: Show and verify the actual sender domain, not only the display name, in mail review workflows.

attacks.name: SMTP header injection
attacks.desc: Unescaped newline characters in an email field can inject additional mail headers.
attacks.prevention: Validate email field values and use a mail library that encodes headers instead of concatenating raw input.

attacks.name: Open relay
attacks.desc: An SMTP server that relays mail for arbitrary senders can be abused to distribute messages.
attacks.prevention: Require authenticated relay clients and restrict permitted sender and recipient domains.

attacks.name: Mailbomb
attacks.desc: Repeated subscription or notification requests can overwhelm a mailbox if abuse controls are weak.

attacks.name: IDN homograph
attacks.desc: Internationalized domain characters can create visually deceptive lookalike names.

attacks.name: Typosquat
attacks.desc: Registering a misspelled domain can misdirect users who mistype a trusted address.

attacks.name: Plus-address abuse
attacks.desc: Plus-address variants may bypass per-email account limits if addresses are not normalized for that rule.

attacks.name: Case-sensitive email bypass
attacks.desc: Case differences in an email address may create duplicate accounts when the application treats equivalent addresses differently.

attacks.name: Email normalization bypass
attacks.desc: Dot rules and Unicode handling can cause account identity checks to disagree about whether two addresses match.
